definition: A language model specifically designed or adapted to handle very large context windows, spanning tens of thousands to millions of tokens.
details: Long-context models enable use cases like reasoning over entire books, codebases, or extensive conversation histories, but require architectural and engineering innovations to remain efficient as context length grows.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Think of it this way: A language model specifically designed or adapted to handle very large context windows, spanning tens of thousands to millions of tokens. And here is the clever part: Long-context models enable use cases like reasoning over entire books, codebases, or extensive conversation histories, but require architectural and engineering innovations to remain efficient as context length grows. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — Long-Context Model — is what makes everything else possible.
